case_number: Civil Appeal No. 1609 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (C) No. 6516/2019)

parties.respondent: M/S Young Friends And Co. & Ors.

summary: The case involved an eviction petition under Section 14 of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, filed by the appellant (landlord) to recover possession of a shop in Connaught Place, alleging unauthorized sub-letting to medical practitioners and firms. The Rent Controller dismissed the petition in 1997, finding no evidence of sub-letting. The Rent Control Appellate Tribunal reversed this, allowing eviction based on sub-letting. The Delhi High Court, exercising Article 227 jurisdiction, set aside the Tribunal's order, holding it was based on conjecture and contrary to evidence showing tenant retained full control. The Supreme Court examined whether the High Court's interference was justified, focusing on legal standards for sub-letting—requiring exclusive possession and monetary consideration. It referenced precedents affirming that mere presence of third parties with permissive use does not constitute sub-letting. The Court found no perversity in the High Court's decision.
final_judgment: Appeal dismissed. The judgment of the Delhi High Court is upheld. The eviction order by the Appellate Tribunal is set aside, and the 1997 order of the Additional Rent Controller dismissing the eviction petition is restored.
